title: How I Audit a Customer Journey — Stage by Stage, Metric by Metric

sections.label: 1 · CAPTURE — HOW JOURNEYS BEGIN
sections.note: Before judging anything downstream, I map every entry point a customer journey can start from.

sections.label: 2 · NURTURE — TOUCHPOINTS & ENGAGEMENT
sections.note: Every touchpoint in the sequence gets checked against its own engagement number, not assumed to be working.

sections.label: 3 · CONVERSION — WHERE INTENT BECOMES ACTION
sections.note: Wherever a journey asks for a decision, that step gets measured on its own conversion rate.

sections.label: 4 · RETENTION — LIFECYCLE AFTER THE SALE
sections.note: The journey doesn't end at the sale, so neither does the audit.

sections.label: 5 · FINDINGS & FIX
sections.note: Every gap gets tied to its stage and its metric, then fixed in order of what's actually losing the most conversion or retention.

nodes.label: Map Every Entry Point: Forms, Ads, Referrals, Events
Check the Metric: Capture Rate and Time to First Touchpoint
Check Every Touchpoint in the Nurture Sequence and What Triggers It
Check the Metric: Engagement Rate and Response Rate by Touchpoint
Check Where and How a Lead Is Asked to Convert
Check the Metric: Conversion Rate at Each Journey Stage
Check What Happens After the Sale: Onboarding, Upsell, Win-Back
Check the Metric: Retention Rate and Repeat Engagement
Log Every Gap Against Its Stage and Its Metric
Rank Gaps by Which Stage Is Losing the Most Conversion or Retention

input_sample.expected: Consistent touchpoint every 2-3 days until conversion or opt-out
input_sample.actual: Sequence stops after touchpoint 2, no re-engagement trigger for cold leads

output_sample.highest_impact_gap: Nurture — sequence dead-ends after touchpoint 2, no re-engagement for cold leads
output_sample.fix_applied: Added a re-engagement branch triggered by no-response after 5 days
